question: Which of the following schemes/programmes is NOT related to microfinance type of initiatives?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ujjawala Scheme.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Ujjawala Scheme is a comprehensive scheme launched by the Ministry of Women and Child Development for the prevention of trafficking and for the rescue, rehabilitation, re-integration and repatriation of victims of trafficking for commercial sexual exploitation — it has nothing to do with microfinance. (उज्ज्वला योजना — मानव तस्करी रोधी योजना)

 

• Jan Dhan Yojana, Jeevika Project (Bihar Rural Livelihoods Promotion Society) and Indira Kranthi Patham (Andhra Pradesh's rural poverty-reduction/SHG programme) are all financial inclusion / microfinance-linked initiatives built around opening bank accounts, credit access, and Self-Help Group (SHG)-based savings and lending.

 

• Since the question asks which is NOT related to microfinance, Ujjawala Scheme stands apart as an anti-trafficking rehabilitation scheme.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Jeevika (BRLPS) was launched in 2007 in Bihar to reduce poverty by promoting SHGs among the rural poor.

 

• Indira Kranthi Patham is the Andhra Pradesh government's poverty eradication programme built on the SHG network, evolved from earlier DWCRA/Velugu initiatives.

 

NOTE

 

• Jan Dhan Yojana (Option 2): The Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana promotes financial inclusion through zero-balance bank accounts, overdraft and micro-credit facilities.

 

• Jeevika Project (Option 3): A Bihar-based SHG microfinance and livelihoods promotion initiative.

 

• Indira Kranthi Patham Programme (Option 4): An Andhra Pradesh SHG-based microfinance and livelihood programme.

question: Bastar Dussehra is celebrated in which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chhattisgarh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bastar Dussehra is a unique, roughly 75-day-long festival celebrated in the Bastar district of Chhattisgarh, unlike the ten-day Dussehra celebrated elsewhere in India. (बस्तर दशहरा — छत्तीसगढ़)

 

• It primarily worships the local deity Goddess Danteshwari (the presiding deity of the erstwhile Bastar royal family) rather than commemorating Lord Rama's victory over Ravana.

 

• The festival is a blend of tribal traditions and rituals and involves rituals like Pat Jatra, Kachin Gadi, and the pulling of a massive wooden chariot (Rath Parikrama) through the town of Jagdalpur.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bastar Dussehra was historically started by the Kakatiya dynasty rulers of Bastar around the 15th century.

 

• Jagdalpur, the district headquarters of Bastar, is the main venue of the celebrations.

 

NOTE

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 1): Celebrates the conventional ten-day Dussehra tied to the Ramlila tradition, notably at Varanasi and Ayodhya.

 

• Haryana (Option 2): Not known for Bastar-style Dussehra celebrations.

 

• Jharkhand (Option 4): Not associated with the Bastar Dussehra tradition.

question: In the MPL 59th Senior National Chess Championship held in Delhi ,Who became India's 78th Grandmaster ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Koustav Chatterjee.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Koustav Chatterjee, a chess player from West Bengal, became India's 78th Grandmaster (GM) by securing his final GM norm at the 59th National Senior Chess Championship held in New Delhi. (कौस्तव चटर्जी — भारत के 78वें शतरंज ग्रैंडमास्टर)

 

• The National Senior Chess Championship is organised by the All India Chess Federation (AICF); the 59th edition (2023) was sponsored by MPL (Mobile Premier League).

 

• To earn the Grandmaster title, a player needs three GM norms and a live rating of 2500 or above, awarded by FIDE, the world chess governing body.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's first Grandmaster was Viswanathan Anand, who earned the title in 1988.

 

• India has seen a rapid rise in the number of Grandmasters in recent years, with several teenage players earning the title.

 

NOTE

 

• G Akash (Option 1): An Indian Grandmaster from Tamil Nadu, but he was not India's 78th GM.

 

• Pranav V (Option 3): An Indian chess player/Grandmaster, not the 78th GM referenced here.

 

• Prithu Gupta (Option 4): An Indian Grandmaster, but not the one who achieved the title at this specific event as the 78th GM.

question: Which of the following Articles says that double jeopardy which says that "no person shall be prosecuted or punished for the same offence more than once"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 20 (2).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 20(2) of the Indian Constitution enshrines the protection against double jeopardy, stating that "no person shall be prosecuted and punished for the same offence more than once." (अनुच्छेद 20(2) — दोहरे दंड से संरक्षण)

 

• Article 20 as a whole provides protection in respect of conviction for offences, covering three safeguards: no ex-post-facto law (Article 20(1)), no double jeopardy (Article 20(2)), and no self-incrimination (Article 20(3)).

 

• This right is available to both citizens and non-citizens, and unlike most Fundamental Rights, it cannot be suspended even during a National Emergency.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The doctrine of double jeopardy has its roots in the Latin maxim "nemo debet bis vexari" (no man should be punished twice for the same offence).

 

• Article 20 falls under Part III of the Constitution dealing with Fundamental Rights.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 21 (2) (Option 1): There is no clause 2 under Article 21; Article 21 itself deals with Protection of Life and Personal Liberty.

 

• Article 19 (1) (Option 2): Guarantees the six fundamental freedoms such as speech and expression, assembly, association, etc.

 

• Article 22 (2) (Option 4): Deals with the right of an arrested person to be produced before a magistrate within 24 hours, part of protection against arrest and detention.

question: The neutral point in the magnetic field of a horizontally positioned bar magnet is the:
option_1: point where the magnetic field changes direction
option_2: point where the magnetic field is the weakest
option_3: point where the magnetic field is the strongest
option_4: point where the magnetic field is zero
solution_text:
The correct answer is point where the magnetic field is zero.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A neutral point is a location around a bar magnet where the magnetic field due to the magnet is exactly cancelled by the horizontal component of the Earth's magnetic field, making the resultant magnetic field zero. (उदासीन बिंदु — चुंबकीय क्षेत्र शून्य)

 

• At a neutral point, a compass needle placed there can point in any direction, since there is no net magnetic force acting on it.

 

• For a horizontally placed bar magnet, neutral points typically lie either on the magnetic equatorial line (when the magnet's north pole points towards geographic north) or on the axial line (when the north pole points towards geographic south).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The concept of neutral points is used in plotting magnetic field lines using a compass needle, and in locating the null points in combined field diagrams.

 

• The Earth's magnetic field itself is often modelled as being produced by an imaginary bar magnet inside the Earth.

 

NOTE

 

• Point where the field changes direction (Option 1): Field lines change direction continuously around a magnet; this does not define a neutral point.

 

• Point where the field is weakest (Option 2): "Weakest" is not the same as "zero"; the neutral point specifically has zero resultant field.

 

• Point where the field is strongest (Option 3): The field is strongest near the poles of the magnet, the opposite of a neutral point.

question: Which is a nutritional disorder caused by vitamin B3 deficiency, leading to clinical manifestations from the skin, gastrointestinal tract and nervous system?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pellagra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pellagra is a nutritional deficiency disease caused by lack of Vitamin B3 (Niacin), classically characterised by the "3 D's": Dermatitis, Diarrhoea and Dementia (skin, gastrointestinal and nervous system involvement). (पेलाग्रा — विटामिन बी3/नियासिन की कमी)

 

• It commonly occurs in populations whose staple diet is maize (corn), which is deficient in niacin and its precursor amino acid tryptophan.

 

• Pellagra can be prevented/treated by including niacin-rich foods such as meat, fish, eggs, and whole grains in the diet.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Vitamin B1 (Thiamine) deficiency causes Beri-Beri; Vitamin C deficiency causes Scurvy; Vitamin B12/iron/folate deficiency causes Anaemia.

 

• The word "pellagra" comes from the Italian "pelle agra", meaning "sour/rough skin".

 

NOTE

 

• Anaemia (Option 1): Caused mainly by deficiency of iron, Vitamin B12 or folic acid, not Vitamin B3.

 

• Beri Beri (Option 3): Caused by deficiency of Vitamin B1 (Thiamine).

 

• Scurvy (Option 4): Caused by deficiency of Vitamin C (Ascorbic acid).

question: With which scientist did William Ramsay show in 1894 that air also contained an element unknown until then, which was named argon?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord Rayleigh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In 1894, chemist William Ramsay, working together with physicist Lord Rayleigh (John William Strutt), discovered that a component of air, after nitrogen and oxygen were removed, was a previously unknown, inert element, which they named Argon (from the Greek "argos", meaning "lazy/inactive"). (आर्गन गैस की खोज — लॉर्ड रैले एवं विलियम रामसे)

 

• This discovery of Argon led Ramsay to go on to discover the other noble gases — Neon, Krypton and Xenon.

 

• William Ramsay was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1904, and Lord Rayleigh was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1904 in the same year, largely for this joint work.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Argon is the third most abundant gas in Earth's atmosphere, after nitrogen and oxygen, making up about 0.93% of air.

 

• The noble gases (Group 18 of the periodic table) are characterised by their very low chemical reactivity.

 

NOTE

 

• Hermann Staudinger (Option 2): A German chemist known as the father of polymer chemistry; won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1953.

 

• Glenn Seaborg (Option 3): An American chemist known for discovering several transuranium elements, including plutonium.

 

• Harold Urey (Option 4): An American chemist known for discovering deuterium (heavy hydrogen), for which he won the 1934 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

question: The Western Ghats and the Eastern Ghats meet at which of the following places in southern India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nilgiri Hills.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats converge at the Nilgiri Hills, located at the tri-junction of Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka. (नीलगिरि पहाड़ियाँ — पश्चिमी और पूर्वी घाट का संगम स्थल)

 

• The name "Nilgiri" means "Blue Mountains", said to be derived from the bluish tinge given by the flowering of the Kurinji (Neelakurinji) shrub or the blue haze over the hills.

 

• The highest peak of the Nilgiris (and of the Western Ghats in Tamil Nadu) is Doddabetta; the region is also home to the hill station of Ooty (Udhagamandalam) and the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, India's first Biosphere Reserve.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, notified in 1986, was the first of India's biosphere reserves and is part of the UNESCO World Network of Biosphere Reserves.

 

• The Palghat (Palakkad) Gap is a natural break in the Western Ghats connecting Tamil Nadu and Kerala, distinct from the Nilgiri junction point.

 

NOTE

 

• Satpura Hills (Option 1): A range in central India, running roughly parallel to the Vindhyas, not connected to the Ghats' meeting point.

 

• Nallamala Hills (Option 2): A hill range in the Eastern Ghats in Andhra Pradesh/Telangana, not the meeting point of the two Ghats.

 

• Mahendragiri Hills (Option 4): Located in the Eastern Ghats in Odisha, unrelated to the Western-Eastern Ghats junction.

question: Which of these is related to public goods?
option_1: The principle of excludability is applicable to its consumption.
option_2: There is a clear link between the producer and consumer which occurs through the payment process.
option_3: Its consumption is rivalrous in nature.
option_4: There is a possibility of free ridership in its consumption.
solution_text:
The correct answer is There is a possibility of free ridership in its consumption.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Public goods are characterised by non-excludability (no one can be excluded from consuming them) and non-rivalry (one person's consumption does not reduce availability for others). (सार्वजनिक वस्तु — निःशुल्क उपयोगकर्ता/फ्री राइडर समस्या)

 

• Because people cannot be excluded even if they don't pay, public goods suffer from the "free rider" problem — individuals can enjoy the benefit of the good without paying for it, e.g. national defence, street lighting, or a public park.

 

• This free-rider problem is a key reason why markets under-provide public goods, and why the government typically has to fund and provide them.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Goods can be classified on two axes — excludability and rivalry — into private goods, club goods, common resources, and public goods.

 

• Common resources (like fisheries) are rivalrous but non-excludable, leading to the "tragedy of the commons", distinct from the free-rider problem of pure public goods.

 

NOTE

 

• Excludability applies (Option 1): Incorrect — public goods are defined by non-excludability, the opposite of what this option states.

 

• Clear producer-consumer payment link (Option 2): Incorrect — because of non-excludability, there is typically no direct payment link between the consumer and provider of a public good.

 

• Rivalrous consumption (Option 3): Incorrect — public goods are non-rivalrous; one person's use does not diminish another's ability to consume it.

question: What is the distance between the goal line and the penalty spot in football?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 12 yards.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Laws of the Game (IFAB), the penalty spot in football is marked 12 yards (approximately 10.97 metres) from the midpoint of the goal line, directly in front of the goal. (पेनल्टी स्पॉट — गोल रेखा से 12 गज की दूरी)

 

• A penalty kick is awarded when a direct free-kick offence is committed by a team inside its own penalty area.

 

• The penalty area itself extends 18 yards from each goalpost and 18 yards into the field of play, while the smaller goal area extends 6 yards.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• During a penalty kick, all players other than the kicker and the goalkeeper must remain outside the penalty area and at least 10 yards from the penalty spot, marked by the penalty arc.

 

• Football's laws are framed and maintained by the International Football Association Board (IFAB).

 

NOTE

 

• 11 yards, 10 yards, 9 yards (Options 1, 3, 4): These do not match the standard distance of the penalty spot from the goal line, which is fixed at 12 yards.

question: Who among the following is NOT a professional Indian Classical Dancer?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shreya Ghoshal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Shreya Ghoshal is a renowned Indian playback singer, not a classical dancer, making her the odd one out among the four names. (श्रेया घोषाल — पार्श्व गायिका, नृत्यांगना नहीं)

 

• Mallika Sarabhai is a well-known Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi dancer, daughter of classical dancer Mrinalini Sarabhai.

 

• Vasundhara Doraswamy and Shovana Narayan (also spelt Shovana Narayanan) are both accomplished Indian classical dancers — Shovana Narayan is particularly noted as a leading Kathak exponent.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Shreya Ghoshal rose to fame after winning the television talent show Sa Re Ga Ma Pa and has since won multiple National Film Awards for playback singing.

 

• Shovana Narayan is a Padma Shri awardee and one of India's foremost Kathak dancers.

 

NOTE

 

• Mallika Sarabhai (Option 1): A professional Bharatanatyam/Kuchipudi classical dancer and activist.

 

• Vasundhara Doraswamy (Option 2): An Indian classical dancer.

 

• Shovana Narayanan (Option 4): A celebrated Kathak classical dancer.

question: The Government of India is providing Ayushman Bharat Yojana, a health scheme. This type of government efforts falls under ________ of the Directive Principles of State Policy.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 47.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 47 of the Indian Constitution, under the Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV), places a duty on the State to raise the level of nutrition and the standard of living of its people and to improve public health. (अनुच्छेद 47 — लोक स्वास्थ्य में सुधार का कर्तव्य)

 

• Government health initiatives such as the Ayushman Bharat Yojana (PM-JAY), which provides health insurance coverage to economically weaker sections, are efforts made in fulfilment of this directive.

 

• Article 47 also directs the State to work towards the prohibition of intoxicating drinks and drugs injurious to health, except for medicinal purposes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ayushman Bharat Yojana (PM-JAY), launched in 2018, is the world's largest government-funded health assurance scheme, providing cover of up to ₹5 lakh per family per year.

 

• The Directive Principles of State Policy are non-justiciable guidelines for governance, borrowed from the Irish Constitution.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 48 (Option 1): Deals with the organisation of agriculture and animal husbandry, including preservation and improvement of livestock breeds and prohibition of cow slaughter.

 

• Article 46 (Option 2): Deals with the promotion of educational and economic interests of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and other weaker sections.

 

• Article 45 (Option 4): Deals with provision for early childhood care and education for children below six years.

question: In which of the following years was the first radio show broadcast in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1923.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The first radio broadcast in India was carried out by the Radio Club of Bombay in June 1923, marking the beginning of organised radio broadcasting in the country. (भारत में पहला रेडियो प्रसारण — 1923)

 

• This was followed by the Calcutta Radio Club later in 1923, and eventually the Indian Broadcasting Company (IBC) began operations in 1927 in Bombay and Calcutta.

 

• The IBC was later taken over by the government and reorganised, eventually becoming All India Radio (AIR) in 1936, and was renamed Akashvani in 1957.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• All India Radio (AIR) is the national public radio broadcaster of India, operating under Prasar Bharati.

 

• India's first television broadcast began in 1959, much later than radio.

 

NOTE

 

• 1936 (Option 2): The year AIR (All India Radio) got its name, not the year of the first radio broadcast.

 

• 1911 (Option 3): Too early; radio broadcasting had not yet begun in India at this time.

 

• 1927 (Option 4): The year the Indian Broadcasting Company was established, not the year of the very first radio broadcast.

question: Ustad Akbar Ali Khan is remembered for his contribution to which of the following musical instruments?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sarod.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ustad Ali Akbar Khan was one of the most celebrated Sarod maestros of Hindustani classical music, belonging to the Maihar gharana. (उस्ताद अली अकबर खान — सरोद वादक)

 

• He was the son and disciple of the legendary musician Allauddin Khan, and is credited with popularising the Sarod on the world stage.

 

• He was honoured with India's second-highest civilian award, the Padma Vibhushan, and received a MacArthur "Genius Grant" Fellowship in the USA.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sarod is a stringed instrument, plucked with a plectrum, known for its deep, resonant sound, and lacks frets unlike the sitar.

 

• Other well-known Sarod players include Amjad Ali Khan, who also belongs to a renowned musical lineage.

 

NOTE

 

• Tabla (Option 1): A percussion instrument; notable maestros include Zakir Hussain and Alla Rakha.

 

• Santoor (Option 2): A trapezoid-shaped hammered string instrument; Pandit Shivkumar Sharma is a noted exponent.

 

• Sitar (Option 3): A plucked string instrument; Pandit Ravi Shankar is its most famous exponent.

question: Who among the following Indian weightlifters won the silver medal in the women's 49 kg division at the World Weightlifting Championships 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Saikhom Mirabai Chanu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Saikhom Mirabai Chanu, the Tokyo Olympics silver medallist weightlifter from Manipur, won the silver medal in the women's 49 kg category at the World Weightlifting Championships 2022 held in Bogotá, Colombia. (साइखोम मीराबाई चानू — विश्व भारोत्तोलन चैंपियनशिप 2022, रजत पदक)

 

• This was a significant comeback for Mirabai Chanu after an injury layoff, and it also secured India a quota place for the Paris 2024 Olympics.

 

• Mirabai Chanu is also an Olympic silver medallist (Tokyo 2020, 49 kg category) and a Commonwealth Games gold medallist.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mirabai Chanu was honoured with the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award and the Padma Bhushan.

 

• India's other notable weightlifters include Sanjita Chanu and Jhili Dalabehera, who have also won international medals.

 

NOTE

 

• Swati Singh (Option 1): Not the silver medallist in this event/category.

 

• Santoshi Matsa (Option 2): Not associated with this specific medal at the 2022 World Championships.

 

• Sanjitha Chanu (Option 3): An accomplished Indian weightlifter, but she is not the one who won this particular silver medal.

question: Which of the following states became the first Indian State to enact 'Right to Health Act 2022'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rajasthan became the first state in India to enact the Right to Health Act, 2022 (passed by the Rajasthan Assembly in March 2023), guaranteeing residents the right to access free OPD and IPD healthcare services, including emergency treatment, at both public and designated private facilities. (राजस्थान — स्वास्थ्य का अधिकार अधिनियम 2022 लागू करने वाला पहला राज्य)

 

• The Act mandates that no patient can be denied emergency treatment or refused admission for lack of payment, and every district is required to set up a District Health Authority to redress grievances.

 

• The law faced protests from private doctors' associations over provisions related to compulsory emergency treatment, which were later addressed through amendments.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rajasthan has also implemented other notable welfare schemes such as the Chiranjeevi Swasthya Bima Yojana, providing cashless health insurance cover.

 

• The Right to Health Act builds on Rajasthan's history of rights-based legislation, following earlier laws like the Right to Information and Right to Guaranteed Delivery of Public Services.

 

NOTE

 

• Punjab (Option 1): Has not enacted a Right to Health Act of this kind.

 

• Haryana (Option 3): No such law has been enacted in Haryana.

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 4): No such law has been enacted in Madhya Pradesh.

question: The Village and Small Scale Industries Committee is also referred to as the ____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karve Committee.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Village and Small-Scale Industries Committee (1955), set up during the Second Five Year Plan period, is popularly known as the Karve Committee, after its chairman Dr. D.G. Karve. (कर्वे समिति — ग्राम एवं लघु उद्योग समिति, 1955)

 

• The committee's recommendations laid emphasis on the promotion of village and small-scale industries to generate employment and support decentralised industrial growth, influencing the industrial policy of the Second Five-Year Plan.

 

• It suggested the creation of institutions to support small industries, which eventually contributed to bodies like the Small Industries Development Organisation (SIDO).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Mahalanobis Model, associated with statistician P.C. Mahalanobis, formed the basis of the Second Five-Year Plan's heavy-industry strategy.

 

• The Chakravarty Committee (1985), headed by Sukhamoy Chakravarty, reviewed the working of the monetary system in India.

 

NOTE

 

• Mahalanobis Committee (Option 1): Associated with the Second Five-Year Plan's growth model and also with reviewing income distribution, not the Village/Small Industries Committee.

 

• Munshi Committee (Option 2): K.M. Munshi was associated with matters like company law reforms, not this committee.

 

• Chakravarty Committee (Option 4): Related to review of the monetary policy system in India (1985), unconnected to village/small-scale industries.

question:
Which of the following is a qualitative measure of credit control used by the Reserve Bank of India?

A) CRR

B) Moral Suasion

C) SLR
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only B.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Moral Suasion is a qualitative (selective) method of credit control used by the RBI, whereby the central bank persuades and advises banks — through informal talks, appeals, or meetings — to follow a particular credit policy without using any coercive/legal power. (नैतिक अनुनय — गुणात्मक साख नियंत्रण उपाय)

 

• CRR (Cash Reserve Ratio) and SLR (Statutory Liquidity Ratio) are both quantitative (general) methods of credit control, as they affect the overall volume of credit uniformly across the banking system, regardless of the purpose of the loan.

 

• Since only Statement B (Moral Suasion) correctly identifies a qualitative tool, while A (CRR) and C (SLR) are quantitative tools, "Only B" is correct.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other qualitative credit control tools include margin requirements, direct action, rationing of credit, and publicity.

 

• Quantitative credit control tools include the Repo Rate, Reverse Repo Rate, Bank Rate, CRR and SLR, which the RBI uses to control the overall money supply.

 

NOTE

 

• Only A (Option 1): Incorrect, since CRR is a quantitative, not qualitative, credit control tool.

 

• Both B and C (Option 3): Incorrect, since SLR (C) is a quantitative tool, not a qualitative one.

 

• Only C (Option 4): Incorrect, since SLR is a quantitative credit control tool, not a qualitative one.

question: What is the crude birth rate of India as per Census 2011?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 21.8%.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Crude Birth Rate (CBR) of India, as commonly cited from Census/SRS 2011 data, stood at approximately 21.8 (per thousand population), reflecting the number of live births per 1,000 population in a year. (भारत की जन्म दर — लगभग 21.8 प्रति हज़ार जनसंख्या)

 

• The Crude Birth Rate is calculated as: (Total number of live births in a year ÷ Mid-year total population) × 1000.

 

• India's crude birth rate has been on a steady declining trend over the decades due to improved family planning, education, and healthcare access.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Crude Death Rate (CDR) of India around the same period was approximately 7 per thousand.

 

• Vital statistics like birth and death rates in India are tracked through the Sample Registration System (SRS), maintained by the Office of the Registrar General of India.

 

NOTE

 

• 20.5%, 20%, 28% (Options 1, 2, 4): These figures do not match the actual crude birth rate recorded around Census 2011, which stood at approximately 21.8.

question: NABARD launched a special pilot project in 2004-05 called ________ mainly to fulfil the credit needs of the small and marginal farmers and tenant farmers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is JLGs.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• NABARD launched the Joint Liability Groups (JLGs) pilot project in 2004-05 to improve the flow of credit to small, marginal, tenant and oral lessee farmers who lack proper title to land and hence find it difficult to access institutional credit individually. (संयुक्त देयता समूह — नाबार्ड पायलट परियोजना 2004-05)

 

• A JLG is an informal group of 4-10 individuals who come together to avail bank credit, either individually or through the group mechanism, against mutual guarantee.

 

• The JLG model helps in providing collateral-free credit to those without formal land titles by leveraging peer support and joint liability instead.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development) was established in 1982 as the apex development bank for rural credit in India.

 

• NABARD is also known for pioneering the Self-Help Group (SHG)-Bank Linkage Programme, one of the largest microfinance programmes in the world.

 

NOTE

 

• MEDP (Option 2): Refers to Micro Enterprise Development Programme, a skill/enterprise training initiative, not the 2004-05 tenant farmer credit pilot.

 

• SGSY (Option 3): Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana, a self-employment scheme for rural poor launched in 1999, later restructured as NRLM, not this pilot project.

 

• BLP programme (Option 4): Refers to bank linkage-related activities but is not the specific name of the 2004-05 pilot for tenant/marginal farmers, which was the JLG initiative.

question: Rajarajeshwara Temple of Tanjore was built by the ruler of which dynasty?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chola.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Rajarajeshwara Temple (also called the Brihadeeswarar Temple), at Thanjavur (Tanjore), was built by the Chola ruler Raja Raja Chola I in the early 11th century (completed around 1010 CE). (राजराजेश्वर मंदिर, तंजौर — चोल वंश, राजराज चोल प्रथम)

 

• Dedicated to Lord Shiva, the temple is renowned for its massive vimana (tower), one of the tallest in India, and is built entirely of granite.

 

• It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, part of the group known as the "Great Living Chola Temples", along with the Gangaikonda Cholapuram and Airavatesvara temples.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Cholas were great patrons of Dravidian temple architecture, and Raja Raja Chola I's son Rajendra Chola I later built the equally magnificent Gangaikonda Cholapuram temple.

 

• The Chola dynasty is also known for administering an extensive naval empire extending to Southeast Asia.

 

NOTE

 

• Pandya (Option 1): Known for temples such as the Meenakshi Temple at Madurai, not the Tanjore temple.

 

• Pallava (Option 2): Known for the Shore Temple and rathas at Mahabalipuram.

 

• Chera (Option 4): A dynasty of ancient Kerala/Tamil region, not associated with the Tanjore temple.

question: Under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, how many minimum days of guaranteed wage employment in every financial year has to be provided to every household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 100.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA), 2005, guarantees 100 days of wage employment in a financial year to every rural household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work. (मनरेगा — 100 दिन की रोजगार गारंटी)

 

• MGNREGA is the world's largest social security and public works programme, aimed at enhancing livelihood security in rural areas.

 

• The scheme is demand-driven, and if employment is not provided within 15 days of the demand, an unemployment allowance must be paid to the applicant.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• MGNREGA mandates that at least one-third of the beneficiaries must be women.

 

• Wages under MGNREGA are paid directly into the bank/post office accounts of workers, promoting financial inclusion and transparency.

 

NOTE

 

• 90, 120, 150 (Options 1, 2, 3): These figures do not match the statutory guarantee under MGNREGA, which is fixed at 100 days per household per financial year.

question: Manju Barggavee won the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award of 2019 for which dance form?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kuchipudi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Manju Bhargavi (Bhargavee), a noted classical dancer, was conferred the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for 2019 in the field of Kuchipudi dance. (मंजू भार्गवी — कुचिपुड़ी नृत्य, संगीत नाटक अकादमी पुरस्कार 2019)

 

• Kuchipudi is a classical dance form that originated in the village of Kuchipudi in Andhra Pradesh, traditionally performed as dance-drama combining rhythmic footwork with expressive storytelling.

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's national academy for music, dance and drama, confers this award annually to recognise excellence in the performing arts.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (Akademi Puraskar) is one of the most prestigious performing arts honours conferred by the Government of India, alongside the Akademi Fellowship (Ratna Sadasya).

 

• Other prominent Kuchipudi exponents include Vempati Chinna Satyam, credited with popularising the form widely across India and abroad.

 

NOTE

 

• Mohiniattam (Option 1): A classical dance form of Kerala, characterised by graceful, swaying movements.

 

• Chhau (Option 2): A semi-classical dance form from eastern India (Odisha, Jharkhand, West Bengal), often involving martial elements and masks.

 

• Kathak (Option 3): A classical dance form of North India, known for its intricate footwork and spins, not the form for which Manju Bhargavi was honoured.

question: Sal, acacia, and bamboo, which are types of Dry Tropical Forest, receive what amount of annual rainfall?
solution_text:
The correct answer is From 51 cm to 151 cm.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dry Tropical Forests (including Tropical Dry Deciduous forests), where trees like Sal, Acacia, and Bamboo are found, typically receive an annual rainfall ranging from about 51 cm to 151 cm (roughly 50-150 cm). (शुष्क उष्णकटिबंधीय वन — 51 से 151 सेमी वार्षिक वर्षा)

 

• These forests are widespread across large parts of the Indo-Gangetic plains, central India, and parts of the peninsula, where rainfall is moderate — not heavy enough to sustain evergreen forest, but sufficient for deciduous tree cover.

 

• Trees in dry tropical forests shed their leaves during the dry season to conserve water, distinguishing them from the wetter tropical evergreen and moist deciduous forest types.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tropical Moist Deciduous forests, by contrast, receive higher rainfall of roughly 150-200 cm.

 

• Tropical Thorn forests, found in very arid regions such as parts of Rajasthan and Gujarat, receive less than 50 cm of rainfall annually.

 

NOTE

 

• 200-250 cm (Option 2): This range is typical of Tropical Moist Deciduous/Semi-evergreen forests, not Dry Tropical forests.

 

• 251 cm or more (Option 3): This heavy rainfall range corresponds to Tropical Evergreen (Rainforest) vegetation.

 

• Below 25 cm (Option 4): This very low rainfall corresponds to arid/desert vegetation, not Dry Tropical (Sal/Acacia/Bamboo) forests.

question: Which of the following ministries of the Government of India has under it the Council of Scientific & Industrial Research (CSIR)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ministry of Science and Technology.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Council of Scientific & Industrial Research (CSIR) functions under the administrative control of the Ministry of Science and Technology, Government of India. (सीएसआईआर — विज्ञान और प्रौद्योगिकी मंत्रालय)

 

• CSIR was established in 1942 and is an autonomous body; interestingly, its ex-officio President is the Prime Minister of India, while the Union Minister of Science and Technology serves as its Vice-President.

 

• CSIR runs a network of national laboratories across India (such as NPL, CDRI, NCL, and CLRI) engaged in scientific and industrial research in diverse fields.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• CSIR is one of the world's largest publicly funded R&D organisations, with a presence in fields ranging from aerospace to biotechnology.

 

• The Ministry of Science and Technology comprises three main departments: Department of Science and Technology (DST), Department of Biotechnology (DBT), and Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (DSIR).

 

NOTE

 

• Ministry of Commerce and Industry (Option 1): Oversees trade, industrial policy and commerce, not CSIR.

 

• Ministry of Earth Sciences (Option 2): Handles agencies like IMD and INCOIS related to weather, ocean and earth sciences, not CSIR.

 

• Ministry of Education (Option 4): Oversees school and higher education institutions, not CSIR, which is a scientific research body.
